mathematics.independent_solution: Use the already-frozen source solution. Appearance alone is underdetermined. Under nonzero free-space plane-wave assumptions, B=(n cross E)/c and n dot E=0. With E along x and n=y, B is along -z so oscillation axis is vertical. With n=(y+z)/sqrt(2), n cross x=(y-z)/sqrt(2), a tilted axis. Nonzero E parallel n=x violates transversality. Complete true set is A/B/C.

option_checks.evidence: Actual figure supplies receiving-crossbar shape but no wave/polarization/matching markers; distinct admissible matched horizontal and tilted waves in the frozen source solution give different B axes.
y cross x=-z. Linear E's time-dependent sign yields back-and-forth motion on the z axis, not a permanent upward or downward vector.
((y+z)/sqrt(2)) cross x=(y-z)/sqrt(2), perpendicular to both E=x and propagation. The quoted tilted line is precisely the magnetic oscillation axis.
n=x and nonzero E along x gives n dot E nonzero. A source-free free-space plane wave cannot have that longitudinal electric field; polarization matching cannot make an invalid wave valid.

mathematics.independent_solution: For propagation y, B_I=(E0/c)*cos(phi)*(x-z)/sqrt(2), so the magnetic axis is tilted and fixed. B_II=(E0/c)*(x*sin(phi)-z*cos(phi)), constant-magnitude rotation in the xz plane; at phi=0 it points -z and at phi=pi/2 it points x, so it is not a z-only oscillator. Ideal dipole voltage is proportional to axial E: V_I proportional to E0*cos(phi)/sqrt(2), V_II proportional to E0*cos(phi). Both are non-identically-zero AC with E0>0 and omega>0. Complete true set is C.

option_checks.evidence: Both voltage claims and wave-I tilted axis are correct, but B_II has nonzero x component at phi=pi/2. It rotates rather than remaining on the z line.
Both magnetic behaviors match the calculation, but the crossbar projections E0*cos(phi)/sqrt(2) and E0*cos(phi) are not identically zero. Non-full polarization matching does not mean no induced AC.
All four parts agree with the independent cross-product/projection calculation: wave I has tilted linear B and AC voltage; wave II has rotating B in xz and AC voltage.
Wave-I claimed x+z axis is parallel to E_I rather than perpendicular. y cross (x+z)=x-z, so the stated wave-I B axis is false even though the remaining claims are true.
